questions.question: Describe SP method in the context of surface geophysical method.
questions.solution_html:
• • Principle: Measuring natural potential differences (Self-Potential) in the earth without an
  • artificial current.
  • • Mechanism: Potentials arise from electrochemical activity or "streaming potential" (water
  • flowing through porous media).
  • • Application: Useful for locating ore bodies, detecting leaks in dams, or mapping shallow
  • groundwater flow.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the physical, chemical, and bacteriological standards specified by / both WHO guidelines and BIS for potable water quality.
questions.solution_html:
• • Physical: Colour, Odor, turbidity, and taste standards (e.g., Turbidity < 5 NTU).
  • • Chemical: Limits for pH (6.5-8.5), Hardness, Iron, and Nitrates. Comparison of BIS (IS 10500)
  • vs. WHO guidelines.
  • • Bacteriological: Requirement for zero E. coli or coliform counts in 100ml samples for safe
  • potable water.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the relationship between groundwater overexploitation, hydraulic / gradient changes and saline water intrusion in coastal and other aquifers, and describe suitable prevention measures.
questions.solution_html:
• Groundwater overexploitation, hydraulic gradient, and saline water intrusion.
  • • Mechanism: Over-pumping lowers the water table, creating a "cone of depression."
  • Marks]
  • • Hydraulic Gradient: Reversal of the gradient causes seawater to flow inland toward the well.
  • [(2 Marks)]
  • • Saline Intrusion: Ghyben-Herzberg relation (freshwater-saltwater interface).
  • • Prevention: Controlled pumping, artificial recharge, and creating hydraulic barriers.
  • Marks]
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the variations in groundwater quality across different Indian provinces.
questions.solution_html:
• Variations in groundwater quality across Indian provinces.
  • • Arsenic: Dominant in West Bengal and Ganga-Brahmaputra plains.
  • • Fluoride: High in arid/semi-arid regions like Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Kerala
  • (Palakkad).
  • • Salinity: Coastal regions (Gujarat/Tamil Nadu) and inland salinity in Punjab/Haryana due to
  • irrigation.
  • • Iron: Common in North-Eastern states and parts of Kerala/Odisha.
questions.final_answer: • Iron: Common in North-Eastern states and parts of Kerala/Odisha
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Illustrate how secondary porosity affects water occurrence in hard rocks.
questions.solution_html:
• • Definition: Porosity created after rock formation via fracturing, jointing, or weathering.
  • Marks]
  • • Crystalline Rocks: Igneous/Metamorphic rocks have zero primary porosity; water is stored
  • only in fractures.
  • • Occurrence: Highly localized; yields depend on fracture connectivity and the thickness of the
  • weathered "saprolite" zone.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe briefly the various types of sub-surface geophysical method.
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly describe various types of sub-surface geophysical methods.
  • • Borehole Logging: Electrical Resistivity logs (Normal/Lateral) to identify aquifers.
  • • Gamma Logging: Identifying clay layers vs. sand.
  • • Sonic/Neutron logging: Measuring porosity and density within the drilled hole.
questions.final_answer: • Sonic/Neutron logging: Measuring porosity and density within the drilled hole
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how high SAR values cause soil dispersion and reduced permeability.
questions.solution_html:
• • Definition: Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR) measures the ratio of $Na^+$ to $Ca^{2+}$ and
  • $Mg^{2+}$.
  • • Process: High Sodium replaces Calcium in clay, causing clay particles to swell and disperse.
  • Marks]
  • • Impact: Dispersed particles block soil pores, destroying soil structure and drastically reducing
  • permeability/infiltration.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe radioactive contamination in groundwater and explain the factors / influencing its occurrence and distribution.
questions.solution_html:
• Radioactive contamination in groundwater.
  • • Sources: Natural (Radon/Uranium leaching from granitic rocks) and Anthropogenic (Mining
  • nuclear waste).
  • • Factors: Geological parent material, pH (solubility), and redox conditions of the aquifer.
  • Marks]
  • • Distribution: High concentrations often found in deep fractured aquifers or near mineralized
  • zones.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Categorize groundwater basins and explain the hydrological boundaries that / define a basin.
questions.solution_html:
• Categorize groundwater basins and explain hydrological boundaries.
  • • Introduction: Definition of a groundwater basin as a hydrogeologic unit containing one or
  • more aquifers.
  • • Categories: Open vs. Closed basins; Rock-bounded vs. Alluvial basins.
  • • Hydrological Boundaries
  • o Physical: Geological contacts, faults, or impermeable strata.
  • o Hydraulic: Groundwater divides (crests in water table), streamline boundaries, and
  • constant head boundaries (large rivers/oceans).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the process of liquid waste disposal and explain how it degrades the / quality of surrounding groundwater.
questions.solution_html:
• Process of liquid waste disposal and groundwater degradation.
  • • Disposal Methods: Septic tanks, rapid infiltration pits, deep well injection, and lagooning.
  • Marks]
  • • Degradation Process: Leaching of pollutants through the vadose zone; formation of a
  • "Contaminant Plume."
  • • Impacts: Nutrient enrichment (Nitrates), Pathogen introduction, Heavy metal accumulation
  • and change in pH/Redox chemistry which can trigger further mineral leaching.
questions.final_answer: and change in pH/Redox chemistry which can trigger further mineral leaching
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
